conceptFrozenBeforeSelection: A computing programme centred on programming, software development, databases, networks and operating systems, algorithms, discrete mathematics, probability and numerical methods. Machine learning, computer vision, neural networks, optimisation and reinforcement learning provide substantial intelligent-systems study. Empirical research and multivariable statistics support evaluation; ethical reasoning and the economic and regulatory study of AI examine responsible engineering. It does not reproduce Delft’s computer-hardware organisation, technical security, dedicated human-computer interaction and graphics, specialist electives or compulsory large software and individual research projects.

selectedCourses.contribution: MandatoryPPD; not a disciplinary substitute.

candidateAssessment.assessment: One strong computing programme is retained. It already sustains programming, algorithms, databases, networks, logic, probability/numerics and all available machine/deep/reinforcement/decision/optimisation learning courses. Reconstructing the old AI option with actual relevant content therefore largely reproduces the core. Linear Systems and Advanced Calculus could change two courses, below four; business foundations, market research, rhetoric and generic sociology cannot be counted as an additional AI-methods sequence. No arbitrary substitutions force distinctness. The separately owned HCI/graphics direction is reassessed as a rejected candidate, not manufactured as a third alternative: product design teaches material consumer-product mechanisms/prototyping, experimental psychology supplies research methods and image processing supplies recognition, but these do not sustain interactive-software design, computer graphics and visual-computing engineering as a distinct24courseprogramme. The remaining course inventory was considered fully; missing outline evidence did not downgrade any course.

alignment.rationale: Formal logic, quantified reasoning, proofs and discrete structures directly overlap; content and credit scope differ.
Programming fundamentals, object-oriented construction and testing overlap directly; UCR uses Python and Delft introduces Java.
No selected course teaches a sustained computer-hardware architecture/organisation sequence.
Single-variable calculus, complex numbers and differential equations directly support mathematical computation; breadth and credits differ.
No selected course requires user-centred software prototyping with generative AI and target-user evaluation. General experiments or physical-product design cannot stand in for it.
Relational data models, normalisation, SQL and queries directly address database management; the full architecture/URI scope differs.
Vectors, matrices, linear transformations and computational linear algebra overlap directly.
Software design/construction, testing and quality assurance overlap directly; languages and engineering-project scale differ.
Data structures, algorithms and performance analysis overlap directly.
Probability, distributions, statistical inference and simulation provide the strongest adequate mathematical counterpart; general research statistics is not substituted for this course.
Network protocols, layered communication and experimental packet analysis directly overlap; UCR also includes operating systems in the same course.
No separate selected course implements Delft’s dedicated collaborative application project. Software Development is already aligned to its strongest design/construction counterpart.
Probabilistic intelligent agents, uncertain/sequential decisions and multi-agent reasoning directly implement an important AI area; not Delft’s full AI introduction.
Greedy/dynamic algorithms, graphs and network-flow optimisation directly address advanced algorithm design.
Operating-system processes, scheduling and memory are substantive within the already-aligned Networks & Operating Systems; no duplicate UCR row or separate second course is created.
Regression/classification, model validation and supervised/unsupervised learning directly overlap.

Selected algorithms already includes computability/complexity, and logic supplies formal reasoning, but no separate selected counterpart covers the formal-language/automata sequence. Related content is acknowledged without duplicating rows.
Software Development includes C++/Haskell paradigms but is already aligned to Software Design; no second counterpart supplies the dedicated concepts/semantics sequence.
AI Ethics addresses values, not technical systems/network/software security, cryptography and authentication.
Image Processing analyses/recognises images. It does not establish computer graphics, geometric scene construction or rendering.
Introductory data cleaning/visualisation is not distributed big-data processing; no selected adequate counterpart.
No selected course is the compulsory15ECexternal-client team software project.
Genuine approved30ECminor remains explicit; no course is equated with unspecified choices.
Neural architectures, deep learning, transformers and text/image prediction directly overlap with an important part of this elective; full generative-AI scope differs.
No selected course sustains bioinformatics; general data methods alone do not establish it.
Programming and AI are taught in distinct selected courses; none specifically implements AI-augmented software-engineering practice.
Individual compulsory15ECresearch remains distinct; the standard optional UCR research element is comparison-only.

boundary: Description-only RL and databases receive full consideration; no inferred algorithm lists, projects or course weighting.19computing/maths courses plus empirical and responsible-engineering complements sustain the core; no invented elective or course-outlining evidence.
